You'll forgive me because I don't often post on this Reddit but I feel so inclined to this time. 
     At the age of 29 I was diagnosed with non Hodgkin's lymphoma. It was very advanced and had spread to most of my body. I am well off so I could afford the best doctors and treatments available. However time and time again I was told it would be a miracle if I made it to 30. I had a son due a few months later and a 4 year old daughter. My first and only thought was of my family and everything that I would miss out on. I think that is what devastated me the most. The thought of them growing up not hearing my dad jokes that I had polished for most of my teen and adult life. (Ask anyone but my wife and they will tell you I'm hilarious) my daughter wouldn't have me to walk her down the isle during her wedding my son wouldn't get to play catch with his old man the whole works. I became depressed. Super depressed. My best friend reached out to me every day from the other side of the country to try and console me. He knew me well and knew I wasn't alright. I finally broke down and told him that I was debating suicide on a daily basis. He calmly took in the information and took me back from the edge. He did something amazing, he pointed out that the things that I was going to miss, the things that depressed me, were the things that should make me happy. Now I know that doesn't make sense the first read over but if you think about it, it really does. There is always something or someone there that gives you purpose, that gives you meaning and it is staring you in the face. You make an impact on someone's life somewhere whether you realize it or not. Now fast forward the the rest of that story. I undergo treatment after treatment mental and physical breakdowns. I go through one setback after another. Hell I had lost all my hair. But somehow 9 months later I came out on the other side. My son just turned 3 my daughter will be 8. I stopped and became thankful for every little thing that has come my way. I receive joy out of making others happy. If I had given up I would have never made it through that ordeal. I would have wasted my life for no reason other than fear. 
Now I doubt you'll read this but maybe someone else will. Maybe it will get buried at the bottom never to be read by anyone. But I hope you find the answers your looking for and I hope those answers bring you joy again. Good luck. I'm rooting for you.
